names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 24 iunie, «Sfântul Ierarh Niceta de Remesiana»; his life gives the name as «Niceta (Nichita)».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 24. јун ст. ст., „Свети Никита, епископ ремесијански“ — Свети is not a rank, епископ is a rank which `types` already carries and ремесијански is the see, so §6 takes all three off and the bare forename is what is left. The «of Remesiana» of the display name is the corpus’s own and §10 reserves it. **THE FOLD IS THE WIDEST THING ON THIS DAY AND IT IS FORCED.** `foldchk.py` returns five other holders of the exact string «Никита» — `nicetas-of-chalcedon`, `nicetas-of-epirus`, `nicetas-of-medikion`, `nicetas-the-chartularius` and `nicetas-the-goth`, every one of them an `sr` form — and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` returns the same five for the gate’s own folded key, so this folder is the sixth. The heading offers nothing to break it with but the see, which §6 strips. A `READ_FOLDS` key is added for it in the same commit, writing the row and registering the fold being two acts.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.07.2026 (24. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети Никита, епископ ремесијански“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 24 June is the same menologion number the Romanian row carries, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed; the Russian and Greek rows stay `undocumented`. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE REFUSAL IS A NARROWING AND NOT A DISAGREEMENT.** This book ends „Упокојио се свети Никита у V веку.“, he reposed in the fifth century. The folder holds `death` earliest 414 and latest **null**, display «after 414», off doxologia’s «a adormit în Domnul puțin după anul 414». A century written as 401 to 500 would **close** that open interval at 500 and move its earliest back to 401 at the same time: half a narrowing and half a widening out of one sentence, and the two books do not disagree at all — «after 414» sits inside the fifth century. There is nothing to widen and a narrowing is refused, so no field moves. The birth, c. 338 off the same Romanian page, is untouched; this book gives no birth and no age. **`types` AND `office` UNTOUCHED, AND THE POEM IS NOT HIS.** The heading gives Свети, not a rank, and епископ, which is the `bishop` the folder carries beside `hierarch` and `hymnographer`; ремесијански is the see and the `office` «Bishop» is already set. **No `office` is invented**: „Столица светог Никите био је град Ремесијан, под којим неки разумеју Пирот.“ — the see of Saint Nicetas was the city of Remesiana, which some understand to be Pirot — is an identification of a place and not a grade, and an `office` goes through the packs’ `offices` branch whose keys are English phrases the data already wrote down. **And the `hymnographer` gains nothing here**: the one piece of verse in the entry is a poem **about** him and not **by** him, „„Каква промена! И како срећна! Дотле непроходне и крваве горе скривају сада разбојнике, обраћене у монахе, питомце мира. Где беху обичаји зверова, тамо је сад лик ангела. Праведник се скрива у пећини, где је раније становао злотвор“.“, which his friend composed to him; §3 keeps it out of `hymns` as it keeps the day’s own verse out, a poem in a life being no troparion, and the folder’s existing `hymnographer` is the Romanian page’s reading and is neither confirmed nor touched by it. **THE FRIEND IS KEPT OUT OF THE PROSE AND PUT HERE, WHICH IS §6’S OWN REMEDY.** The entry opens „Друг и врсник светог Павлина Нолског“, the friend and coeval of Saint Paulinus of Nola, with a cross-reference to 23 January, and goes on „Какву је промену учинио свети Никита међу Словенима, најбоље показује песма, коју је свети Павлин спевао Никити:“ `ls saints | grep -i paulin` returns six folders, of which `paulinus-of-nola` is the man — and **its display name is «Paulinus the Merciful», three words, which `usableName` accepts, so the page’s own cross-linker would match it in prose and `related-floor.test.mjs` would demand a row in both directions.** Measured with `.tmp/sr-prosechk.mjs` before a word was drafted, which is the instrument this sitting built for exactly the trap that bit twice on an emperor. The name is therefore left out of the paragraph below and written here instead, and **nothing was added to `scripts/related-floor-exclusions.json`**. Whether a friend and coeval whose poem the book quotes should carry a `related` row on both folders is a reading worth making and is the author’s: this reader did not open the 23 January page, so it has read one side of the acquaintance only. **WHAT THIS BOOK HAS AND THE ROMANIAN PAGE DOES NOT.** „Изгледа да је био Словен, и као такав да је проповедао Јеванђеље међу Словенима у области нишко-пиротској.“ — it seems he was a Slav, and as such preached the Gospel among the Slavs in the Niš-Pirot region — and „Столица светог Никите био је град Ремесијан, под којим неки разумеју Пирот.“ The «Изгледа да» is the book’s own hedge, it seems that, and it is kept as a hedge in the prose rather than reported as a fact. **No `locations`**: Remesiana, Pirot and the Niš-Pirot region are named in clauses, and the identification of the see with Pirot is one this book attributes to some and not to itself. „Поред своје мисионарске службе свети Никита је написао и неколико књига, као шест књига о вери, књигу о палој девојци(која је многе побудила на покајање).“ gives him six books on the faith and a book on the fallen girl which moved many to repentance; the Romanian page’s own account of his writing stands beside it untouched. **NO ROWS.** The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse, and this day also carries a poem, which is not a hymn either and is dealt with on the second entry. THE VERSE IS NOT USED. The ПЕСМА for 24 June is twenty lines on the Forerunner alone and nothing on the bishop or the seven brothers: it has the knife of Herod miss the child and not miss the child’s father, has angels for the orphan’s shepherds and guardians, and calls him the end of the great prophets and the beginning of God’s apostles. It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not an entry’s account, so §3 of this wave’s brief puts it in no field and in no life, and it is recorded here instead. **For the second day running the verse treats one entry of three or four and ignores the rest**, which is worth the line: the verse is no index of what a day holds.

hymns.text: Propovăduitor şi apărător al dreptei credinţe la multe neamuri te-ai arătat, Sfinte Ierarhe Niceta şi cu smerenie ai câştigat pe cele înalte, bine chivernisind darul. Pentru aceasta, Părintele nostru, roagă pe Hristos Dumnezeu să ne ocrotească de tot răul şi să ne mântuiască.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Niceta de Remesiana, glas 4.

english.text: A preacher and a defender of the right faith among many nations thou wast shown to be, O holy hierarch Nicetas, and in humility thou didst gain the things on high, husbanding well the gift given thee. Therefore, our father, pray Christ God to shelter us from every evil and to save us.
